title: Why Cities Stay Hot After Sunset
titleZh: 城市為何在日落後仍然炎熱
summaryZh: 城市材料會在白天吸熱並於夜間釋放，加上樹蔭不足與人為熱源，形成夜間熱島效應。

sentences.text: On a summer afternoon, a city and the countryside around it may both feel dangerously hot.
sentences.zh: 夏日午後，一座城市與周圍鄉間可能都熱得危險。

sentences.text: After sunset, however, fields often cool quickly while city streets continue to release heat for hours.
sentences.zh: 然而日落之後，田野通常迅速降溫，城市街道卻會持續數小時釋放熱量。

sentences.text: This difference is part of what scientists call the urban heat island effect.
sentences.zh: 這種差異是科學家所稱都市熱島效應的一部分。

sentences.text: Dark roofs and asphalt absorb a large share of the sun's energy during the day.
sentences.zh: 深色屋頂和柏油路面在白天吸收大量太陽能量。

sentences.text: Because these materials store heat well, they act like slow batteries once the air begins to cool.
sentences.zh: 由於這些材料很會儲熱，空氣開始降溫後，它們就像緩慢放電的電池。

sentences.text: Tall buildings can also reduce airflow and trap warm air between narrow streets.
sentences.zh: 高樓也會減少空氣流動，讓暖空氣困在狹窄街道之間。

sentences.text: Cars, air conditioners, kitchens, and industrial equipment add waste heat to the same space.
sentences.zh: 汽車、空調、廚房與工業設備又把廢熱排入同一空間。

sentences.text: Rural areas usually have more plants, which cool their surroundings as water evaporates from leaves and soil.
sentences.zh: 鄉間通常有更多植物，水分從葉片與土壤蒸發時會冷卻周遭環境。

sentences.text: A neighborhood with few trees loses both that cooling process and the immediate protection of shade.
sentences.zh: 樹木稀少的社區，同時失去這種降溫過程與樹蔭的直接保護。

sentences.text: The effect is not equal across a city, because building density and access to green space vary greatly.
sentences.zh: 熱島效應在城市中並不平均，因為建築密度與綠地取得程度差異很大。

sentences.text: In many places, lower income districts have fewer trees and more exposed pavement than wealthier districts.
sentences.zh: 在許多地方，低收入地區的樹木比富裕地區少，裸露路面則更多。

sentences.text: Hot nights are especially harmful because the human body gets less time to recover from daytime heat.
sentences.zh: 炎熱夜晚尤其有害，因為人體從白天高溫中恢復的時間更少。

sentences.text: Planting trees can help, but young trees need years of care before they provide a broad canopy.
sentences.zh: 種樹能有所幫助，但幼樹需要多年照顧才能形成寬廣樹冠。

sentences.text: Cities can also use lighter roofs, shaded walkways, and surfaces that allow water to enter the ground.
sentences.zh: 城市也能採用淺色屋頂、有遮蔭的步道，以及能讓水滲入土壤的鋪面。

sentences.text: No single change removes urban heat, but many small design choices can make summer nights safer.
sentences.zh: 沒有任何單一改變能消除都市高溫，但許多小型設計選擇能讓夏夜更安全。

questions.q: Why do city streets often stay warm after sunset?
options: Urban materials slowly release heat stored during the day
City streets receive sunlight for more hours
Nighttime winds always move toward the countryside

questions.q: How do plants help cool an area?
options: They block all movement of warm air
They cool the surroundings as water evaporates
They turn heat directly into light

questions.q: Why are hot nights particularly dangerous?
options: Most air conditioners stop working after dark
Roads become harder to see in the heat
The body has less time to recover from daytime heat
